name: Pilatus PC-7
summary: Swiss turboprop basic trainer derived from the P-3, used by dozens of air forces and displayed by private owners; the PT6A-powered trainer that preceded the PC-9 and T-6.

wings: Low, straight, tapered wing with squared-off tips
Slight dihedral on the outer panels
engines: Single PT6A turboprop with a three-blade propeller
Slim, long cowl with a chin scoop and exhaust stacks
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long bubble canopy, rear seat higher
Rounded dorsal hump behind the canopy
tail: Swept fin with a dorsal fillet
Horizontal stabilizer mounted on the fuselage

tellTales: Slim turboprop trainer with a three-blade propeller and a long tandem canopy
Long cowl with a chin scoop and exhaust stubs ahead of a low, straight wing
Stepped tandem seating on a small military trainer

confusedWith.howToTell: The PC-9 has a four-blade propeller and a longer, more powerful engine; the PC-7 has a three-blade propeller and a shorter cowl.
The Tucano has a short snub nose and a long flat canopy; the PC-7 has a longer nose and a more upright canopy.
The T-6 Texan II has a four-blade propeller, a larger tail and a taller canopy; the PC-7 has three blades and a lower profile.
The SF.260 is a piston airplane with tip tanks; the PC-7 is a turboprop without tip tanks.
